title: Two Swaps, One Total: How Much Money Do They Have? | AMC 8-Style Level 4

scenes.visual: Two characters as simple labeled wallets/piggy banks: 'Ali' (green) and 'Bea' (purple), with '?' amounts. Line 1: a coin arrow Ali→Bea, '=' sign. Line 2: a coin arrow Bea→Ali, '×2'. Line 3: Vantee title card.
lines: Two friends, two different money swaps, and two clues.
Can we find how much money they have together? Let's draw it out!
Hi, I'm Vantee! Let's solve this with bars.

scenes.visual: Question text left, Ali and Bea wallets right. Line 2: arrow Ali→Bea '20% of Ali's money' then both wallets 'same'. Line 3: tag 'OR, instead:' then arrow Bea→Ali '$10', Ali '= 2 × Bea'. Line 4: 'together = ?'. Line 5: choice chips 90, 150, 200, 240, 300.
lines: Here's the question.
If Ali gives Bea twenty percent of his money, they will have the same amount.
If instead Bea gives Ali ten dollars, Ali will have twice as much as Bea.
How many dollars do our two friends, Ali and Bea, have together?
Here are the five choices.

scenes.visual: Line 1: two separate cards side by side 'Clue 1' and 'Clue 2', each starting from the same two wallets; 'instead' highlighted. Line 2: tag 'goal: Ali + Bea'.
lines: There are two clues. The word instead means each one starts fresh, from the same amounts again.
We want the total: Ali's money plus Bea's money.

scenes.visual: Pause card with countdown ring; question visible.
lines: Pause the video and give it a go. I'll wait!

scenes.visual: Bar model. Line 1: tag 'draw a bar model'. Line 2: '20% = 1/5' (\dfrac); Ali's bar split into 5 equal green parts. Line 3: one part slides from Ali's bar to Bea's side; Ali now 4 parts. Line 4: Bea's bar after the gift is 4 parts long, matching Ali (dashed '=' line). Line 5: remove the gifted part: Bea's starting bar = 3 parts (purple).
lines: Welcome back! Let's draw a bar model.
Twenty percent is one fifth. So split Ali's money into five equal parts.
Clue one: Ali gives one part to Bea. Now Ali has four parts.
They have the same amount, so Bea now has four parts too.
One of those parts was Ali's gift. So Bea started with three parts.

scenes.visual: Fresh bars: Ali 5 parts, Bea 3 parts. Lines 1–2: '$10' block slides from Bea's bar onto Ali's: Ali '5 parts + 10', Bea '3 parts − 10'. Line 3: Bea's bar doubled underneath: '6 parts − 20'. Line 4: row '5 parts + 10 = 6 parts − 20'. Line 5: cancel 5 parts from both sides → '1 part − 20 = 10'. Line 6: '1 part = 30'. Line 7: bars labeled 'Ali 5 × 30 = 150', 'Bea 3 × 30 = 90'. Line 8: answer badge '150 + 90 = 240', chime at end, choice D highlighted.
lines: Clue two, starting fresh: Bea gives Ali ten dollars.
After the swap, Ali has five parts plus ten, and Bea has three parts minus ten.
Twice Bea's money is six parts, minus twenty dollars.
Ali has twice as much, so five parts plus ten equals six parts minus twenty.
Take five parts from both sides. One part minus twenty is ten.
So one part is thirty dollars.
So Ali has five parts, one hundred fifty dollars, and Bea has three parts, ninety dollars.
Together, that's two hundred forty dollars. Choice D!
Let's check clue one. Twenty percent of one hundred fifty is thirty.
Ali keeps one hundred twenty, and Bea ends up with one hundred twenty.
Clue two: Ali ends with one hundred sixty, and Bea drops to eighty.
One hundred sixty is twice eighty. Both clues work!

scenes.visual: Equation rows right. Line 1: 'Ali = a, Bea = b'. Line 2: 'a − a/5 = b + a/5' (\dfrac). Line 3: 'b = a − 2a/5 = 3a/5'. Line 4: 'a + 10 = 2(b − 10)'. Line 5: '= 6a/5 − 20'. Line 6: 'a/5 = 30 → a = 150, b = 90'. Line 7: small text 'when bars get messy'.
lines: Here's another way. Use letters: a for Ali's dollars and b for Bea's.
Clue one: a minus a fifth of a equals b plus a fifth of a.
So b is a minus two fifths of a. That's three fifths of a.
Clue two: a plus ten equals two times, b minus ten.
That's six fifths of a, minus twenty.
So one fifth of a is thirty. Then a is one hundred fifty, and b is ninety. Same answer!
When would you pick this way? When the parts don't come out even, letters still work.

scenes.visual: Choice chips row; each turns red with a note. Line 1: chip A '90 = Bea only', chip B '150 = Ali only'. Line 2: chip E '2 × 150 = 300'. Lines 3–4: chip C '200 = 8 parts of 25'. Line 5: 'Ali 125, Bea 75'. Line 6: '135 and 65'. Line 7: '2 × 65 = 130 ≠ 135' red. Line 8: chip D '240' green.
lines: Now the traps. Choices A and B, ninety and one hundred fifty, are each person alone.
Choice E, three hundred, doubles Ali's money instead of adding Bea's.
Choice C, two hundred, looks friendly. Let's test it.
The total is eight parts, so one part is twenty-five.
Then Ali has one hundred twenty-five, and Bea has seventy-five.
After Bea gives ten, that's one hundred thirty-five and sixty-five.
Twice sixty-five is only one hundred thirty. Not a match!
Only two hundred forty passes both clues.

scenes.visual: Card: 'If Ali gives Bea 25% of his money, they have the same. If instead Bea gives Ali $6, Ali has 3 times as much as Bea. Together = ?'.
lines: Ready for a challenge? If Ali gives Bea twenty-five percent of his money, they have the same amount.
If instead Bea gives Ali six dollars, Ali has three times as much as Bea.
How much do they have together?

scenes.visual: Pause card, countdown, variant text visible.
lines: Pause the video, and go for it!

scenes.visual: Bars per line: '25% = 1/4' Ali 4 parts; gives 1 → 3; Bea 3 − 1 = 2 parts; 'Ali 4 parts + 6 = 3 × (2 parts − 6)'; '= 6 parts − 18 → 2 parts = 24 → 1 part = 12'; 'Ali 48, Bea 24'; answer badge '48 + 24 = 72' chime at end of that line; check '54 = 3 × 18 ✓'.
lines: Let's check. Twenty-five percent is one quarter, so Ali has four parts.
He gives one part and keeps three.
Bea ends with three parts, so she started with two.
Clue two: four parts plus six equals three times, two parts minus six.
That's six parts minus eighteen. So two parts make twenty-four, and one part is twelve.
Ali has forty-eight, and Bea has twenty-four.
Together, they have seventy-two dollars!
Check: after Bea gives six, it's fifty-four and eighteen. Fifty-four is three times eighteen!
Now clue one: forty-eight minus twelve is thirty-six, and twenty-four plus twelve is thirty-six.
If you got seventy-two, wonderful work!

scenes.visual: Summary card: 'percent → equal parts', 'each clue → one balance', 'solve for one part'.
lines: Here's the big idea to remember.
Turn the percent into equal parts, and turn each clue into a balance.
Find what one part is worth, and everything else falls into place.
I'm Vantee. Keep balancing, and I'll see you next time!
